name: EP-13 Resident Fee Structure and Online Collection (Backlog)
w: The MVP bills one thing: monthly rent per sharing type, with cash or UPI recorded by hand. Real hostels and PGs also charge mess, electricity and maintenance, take a refundable deposit, give discounts, charge late fees, accept advances and settle up on move-out, and owners want residents to pay online. This epic builds the full fee structure on top of the MVP's rules: amounts in paise, invoices that never change once issued, append-only payments and balances derived at read time.

out: No wallets, EMIs or multi-currency. Reminders and receipts sent to residents are EP-11. Charging hostels for the software is EP-14.
dod: Not started. Each task has its own acceptance criteria. Invoices stay immutable and payments append-only throughout; every money rule is enforced in the database with integration tests.

name: Fee heads: itemised charges beyond rent
w: Most PGs bill rent plus mess, maintenance and sometimes laundry or Wi-Fi. Today an invoice holds a single amount. Charges need to be itemised so residents see what they pay for and owners can price each part separately.
ac: Owners define fee heads per hostel (rent is built in; for example mess, maintenance, Wi-Fi, laundry), each recurring monthly or one-time, priced per sharing type or flat per resident, with effective dates like rates today
Invoices gain line items (head, description, nights, rate, amount); the invoice amount is the sum of its lines, enforced in the database
generate_invoices bills every recurring head, prorated by nights like rent; an allocation can opt a resident out of a head (for example no mess)
Existing single-amount invoices keep working and show as one 'Rent' line
Printed invoices list each line

name: One-time and ad-hoc charges
w: Admission fees, key replacement, damage and extra services are charged once, outside the monthly cycle.
ac: Owners or staff add a charge to a resident with a head, amount, date and note
Pending charges are added to the resident's next monthly invoice, or invoiced on their own when the owner chooses 'bill now'
An admission fee can be configured to apply automatically on a resident's first allocation
A charge is voided with a reason before it is invoiced; after that it follows invoice voiding

name: Metered electricity billing per room
w: Many PGs charge electricity by the room's sub-meter and split it among the occupants. Owners currently do this on paper.
ac: Record a meter reading per room per month (opening and closing units); a reading lower than the previous one is refused
Units multiplied by a per-unit rate become a charge split among the room's occupants by nights held in the period
The split is shown on each resident's invoice line (units, rate, share)
A missing reading is flagged before invoices are generated instead of being billed as zero

name: Security deposit ledger
w: Deposits are refundable money held for the resident, not income. Mixing them with rent hides how much the owner owes back and makes move-out disputes common.
ac: A deposit amount is set per hostel and sharing type, with a per-resident override, and requested when a resident is allocated
Deposit receipts, deductions (with reason) and refunds are append-only ledger rows separate from invoices; the held balance is derived
Deposits never count as collected rent on the dashboard; a separate 'deposits held' figure is shown
The resident profile shows deposit paid, deductions and balance held

name: Discounts and concessions
w: Owners give sibling discounts, long-stay discounts and one-off waivers. Recording them as a lower rent override loses the reason and the full price.
ac: A discount is a percentage or fixed amount on a head, for one month or recurring between dates, with a reason
Owners create discounts; staff can only see them
Discounts appear as negative lines on the invoice, and an invoice can never go below zero
A report lists discounts given per month

name: Late fees with grace period and waiver
w: Late fees encourage paying on time, but they must be predictable and fair, and an owner must be able to waive one.
ac: Per hostel: grace days after the due date, and a late fee that is a fixed amount or a per-day amount with a cap
Late fees are added as their own charge, never by editing an issued invoice, and only once per invoice per rule
Owners waive a late fee with a reason; the waiver is recorded
Applying late fees is idempotent and runs on a schedule or from a button, in India's calendar

name: Advances and resident credit balance
w: Today a payment larger than what is due is refused. Residents often pay ahead or pay a round amount. That money should become a credit applied to the next invoice, not be turned away.
ac: A payment beyond the open balance, or with no invoice, is accepted as resident credit (an append-only ledger)
When an invoice is issued, available credit is applied automatically and recorded as an allocation of credit to that invoice
Credit can be refunded with a mode and reference; balances can never go negative
Balances, the fee list and the dashboard show credit separately from dues; overpayment between two collectors at once stays impossible

name: Move-out settlement statement
w: When a resident leaves, the owner and resident need one statement: final month's rent for nights stayed, other charges, deposit deductions, credit, and the amount to refund or collect.
ac: Vacating a bed offers a settlement: re-bills the final month by nights held (voiding and regenerating as today), lists unpaid dues, deposit held, deductions and credit
The settlement shows a single net figure: refund to the resident or amount still owed
Confirming records the deposit deductions and refund, or the amount due, in the ledgers
A printable settlement statement in the invoice style

name: Sequential, GST-ready invoice and receipt numbers
w: Invoice numbers today are the first 8 characters of the record id: not sequential, and they can repeat. Once a hostel shows a GSTIN, Indian GST rules expect consecutive numbering, unique within a financial year, of at most 16 characters. Changing numbering after go-live is painful, so it comes first.
ac: Each hostel has an invoice series and a receipt series per financial year (April to March), for example INV/2026-27/0001, assigned in the database with no gaps from concurrent inserts
A void invoice keeps its number; regenerating creates a new number
Numbers are at most 16 characters and unique per hostel and year, enforced by a unique index
Fee heads carry a tax rate and SAC code; invoices for a hostel with a GSTIN show taxable value, tax and SAC per line, rounded to the rupee
Confirm the GST treatment of hostel rent and food with a chartered accountant before enabling tax lines
out: No e-invoicing (IRN) integration; that applies only above the turnover threshold.

name: Online rent collection through a payment gateway
w: Owners want residents to pay by UPI or card from a link instead of chasing cash. The gateway's confirmation, not the browser, is what records a payment.
ac: Owners connect their own gateway account (Razorpay or Cashfree; choose one first) in settings; keys are stored server-side only and never sent to the browser
Each open invoice can produce a payment link or UPI QR for its balance; the resident pays without an account
A signed webhook records the payment idempotently (the gateway payment id is unique), with mode 'online' and the gateway reference; partial and failed payments are handled
Refunds made in the gateway are mirrored as voided payments or credit, never silently
A reconciliation view lists gateway settlements against recorded payments, including gateway fees
Webhook signature checks and replayed or forged events are covered by tests
out: No card data ever touches our servers; no in-app wallet.

name: Cheque payments with clearance status
w: Some residents and parents still pay by cheque. A cheque is not money until it clears, and a bounced cheque must undo the payment.
ac: Payment mode 'cheque' with cheque number and bank, recorded as pending
Pending cheques do not reduce the balance until marked cleared
A bounced cheque is voided with the reason recorded, and can carry a bounce charge (E13-T2)
A list of pending cheques by deposit date

name: Collection reports and exports
w: Owners reconcile cash daily and file accounts monthly. The fee list answers 'who owes what' but not 'what came in, how'.
ac: Daily collection report by payment mode and collector, matching the dashboard's collected figure
Dues ageing: amounts outstanding 0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and 90+ days
Monthly fee register (invoices, lines, payments, credits, deposits) exported as CSV for an accountant
Every export runs in the database without the 1000-row API cap
